summary: The plan is stamped (planning) as soon as it loads and becomes running only when the gate review passes; vloop run resumes acceptance with no plan session whenever a plan has not passed its gate review. A runs test now pins that the resumed acceptance folder is owned and its sessions counted.
verified: vloop task gate T2 logic (sh .vloop/state/gates/T2/gate.sh) exited 0 and printed gate T2: ok; go test ./internal/runs ./cmd/vloop passed.
notes: Earlier attempt's plan.go work is unchanged in the tree. The review's finding that the resumed folder is not owned came from reading logOwns, which only serves shell-loop loop.log folders; vloop folders are owned by sitting under .vloop/state/runs/<run id>/, so no code change was needed, only the new test TestVloopResumedAcceptanceFolderIsOwned. Domain docs for the lifecycle and resume are T10's.
